source_messages.body_text: Bloom Energy built its entire bull case on a backlog anchored by one massive data center project, and now a pipeline delay outside its control is forcing investors to ask whether 2027 and 2028 revenue targets were ever as solid as the pitch sounded.

discovered_facts.proposition: 据报道，Bloom Energy最大的单一燃料电池部署项目因Bloom无法控制的管线延误而面临延期。

executions.pnl_basis: realized net P&L from owned exit allocations; no mark-to-market estimate

delta_candidates.proposition: Oracle已向Blue Owl Capital就New Mexico Project Jupiter计算园区发出force majeure通知。
Oracle寻求在该园区无法按计划于2028年投产时推迟或调整部分付款。
Project Jupiter被描述为2.45GW计算园区，属于更广泛的Stargate AI建设项目，项目规模约1650亿美元。
Bloom Energy据报道将为该项目提供2.5GW燃料电池容量。
该项目面临关键燃气管线约六个月的延误以及水权争议。
与该项目相关的约180亿美元建设债务交易价格低于面值90美分。
Oracle表示项目仍按计划推进，并称force majeure通知是大型开发项目中保护合同权利的标准步骤。

expert_trade.expectation_delta: Oracle正式发出force majeure通知并寻求在2028年投产延误时推迟或调整付款，叠加关键燃气管线约六个月延误和水权争议，使与Bloom据称相关的2.5GW项目的付款、交付、验收和现金转换时点更不确定。Oracle称项目仍按计划推进，因此这不是已确认取消，但相较事件前预期，项目执行和实现确定性已下修。
expert_trade.prior_expectation: BE的事件前预期包含Oracle大型数据中心关系和持续的AI大负荷项目兑现：Bloom已披露最多2.8GW的Oracle主服务协议、约1.2GW已签约并部署容量，以及依赖项目融资、许可、交付和验收兑现的FY2026增长指引。基线并未包含Oracle针对该旗舰项目正式采取付款保护措施。
expert_trade.reason: 正式force majeure通知相对此前传闻和正常执行基线构成实质Surprise；2.45GW项目及据报道的2.5GW Bloom燃料电池容量使其对客户集中度、收入时点和营运资本具有Materiality。传导路径为项目许可/燃料与付款风险上升→Bloom部署、验收及收款时点延后或条件化→收入、现金流和FY2026后续持续期预期下修。Oracle的按期表述限制了下行幅度但不足以消除风险，因此形成SHORT交易判断。

novelty.reason: E40和E41仅记录Oracle据报道寻求force majeure及付款延期，状态为传闻；当前消息确认Oracle已向Blue Owl Capital发出正式通知，并新增项目规模、Bloom容量、管线延误、建设债务和Oracle对项目进度的正式表述。

policy.reason: 虽然事件对Project Jupiter及Bloom的项目兑现风险具有实质意义，但未确认Green Chile管线及其与原有燃料里程碑的越窗关系，也未明确Bloom Energy部署取消、承诺容量缩减、backlog或收入变化，因此未满足现行Policy的具体触发边界。

 The 2028 launch of a massive compute campus in the Southwest is now subject to revised financial terms after Oracle issued a force majeure notice to developer Blue Owl Capital. The 2.45GW Project Jupiter site, part of the broader Stargate AI buildout, has faced permitting hurdles including a six month delay for a critical gas pipeline and disputes over water rights. This maneuver seeks to shield the company from rising expenses if the facility misses its opening date, while associated construction debt of $18B is already trading below 90 cents on the dollar.
Oracle maintains that the project is on schedule and characterizes the notice as a standard step to preserve contractual rights in large-scale developments. The news triggered a decline of around 5% in Oracle shares and weighed on Bloom Energy, which is providing 2.5GW of fuel cell capacity for the $165B project. Local opposition in Doña Ana County has increased scrutiny over environmental impacts while New Mexico state officials draft new regulations for the data center industry.

source_messages.body_text:
ORLANDO, Florida, Sept 24 (Reuters) - The global bond rout continued on Thursday, pushing many key yields around the world to new multi-decade highs. Stock markets around the world felt the heat, although the S&P 500 and Nasdaq staged late rallies to end flat, while oil and the dollar marched higher.

In my column today, I look at the dollar's resurgence and soaring bond yields ​in the context of the US Treasury's recent forays into the FX and bond markets. Right now, "the house" — as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent referred to himself ‌recently — is not winning.

Today's Key Reads

Today's Talking Points:

No, Mr Bond, I expect you to die

The global bond ​selloff got ugly this week. The rise in yields on Wednesday — ostensibly for "good" reasons of strong business activity data — was exceptional, and pointed to a more worrying breakdown in sentiment. There was ​little relief on Thursday. Yields are at multi-decade highs in the US, Europe and Japan, but this isn't drawing in buyers en masse. Bond market volatility is now surging too, another reason many investors might sit it out a bit longer.

Demand at yesterday's 5-year US bond auction was the lowest in nine years, and the premium demanded by buyers who did show up was one of the highest ever. Today's 7-year ​auction was also extremely weak. As BofA analysts put it, "the price action likely highlights that investors are not yet comfortable owning bonds in the environment of a Fed restarting the ​hiking cycle, continued conflict in the Middle East, and a resilient US economy and consumer."

An unbridgeable US-China gap

Huge fanfare, pomp, and ceremony, but not much substance when it comes to the big issues of the ‌day. Is ⁠that a harsh but fair assessment of how the Trump-Xi summit will pan out? True, the US-China trade truce could be extended for another two months to January, and the two sides will agree to further dialogue on AI. But from a market and investment perspective, that's about it.

One ironic market curiosity: it is perhaps fitting that on the day Trump and Xi tried to bridge divides and close gaps between the two superpowers, the spread between the two countries' bond yields widened to a record 350 basis points. US borrowing costs are soaring ​in the face of high inflation, while China’s ​are sliding as the threat of deflation ⁠continues to stalk the economy. Neither side is "winning" on that front.

Data center blues

Oracle on Thursday declared "force majeure" on a massive AI data center project, seeking to protect itself from soaring costs from potential delays in securing power for the "Project Jupiter" venture in New Mexico. Oracle's credit rating ​sits one notch above junk, and its total debt stands at around $140 billion. Shares fell to a seven-week low on Thursday.

But this ​goes well beyond Oracle. ⁠The industry-wide AI capex spend runs into the trillions of dollars, and is increasingly being financed by debt, leasing and other off-balance sheet structures. Many investors were already nervous about the vast cost of building the data centers needed to power the artificial intelligence revolution. This potentially pours fuel on these flames.

What could move markets tomorrow?
